Question: One side of an equilateral triangle of height \(24\) lies on line \(\ell.\) A circle of radius \(12\) is tangent to \(\ell\) and is externally tangent to the triangle. The area of the region exterior to the triangle and the circle and bounded by the triangle, the circle, and line \(\ell\) can be written as \(a\sqrt{b} - c\pi,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are positive integers and \(b\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(a + b + c?\)
